transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, doctor. Thank you. Well, I came in because I keep having these evenings where... I just eat a really large amount of food. I'll go and buy a family-size takeout order after work, and usually I'll add chips or some bakery things from the store to it. And then I end up eating most of it myself before I even seem to register how much is actually gone.
After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself vomit, taking laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything. And I definitely don't exercise like that. I usually just... sit there feeling incredibly full and upset with myself, but I don't do anything to try and get rid of the calories.
How often do these episodes of eating large amounts of food happen? For example, do they occur weekly, a few times a week, or less frequently?

Well, I actually keep a journal, and... looking back through it, there has barely been a week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks, it happens several times.
During these episodes when you're eating large amounts of food, do you feel like you have control over how much you're eating, or does it feel like you can't stop even if you wanted to?

It definitely feels like I can't stop. It's... well, once I start eating, it's like this awful switch flips. I can literally be sitting there thinking to myself, *Taylor, put it away, you've had enough*, but my hands just keep opening containers. It's like I'm not even the one in charge of my own body at that point. I just can't stop myself.
When these episodes happen, is there usually something bothering you emotionally beforehand—like stress, sadness, anxiety, or anger—that seems to trigger the eating?

I'm not really sure if there's a specific emotion or trigger before it happens. I haven't really noticed a pattern like that. I mean, I have stress from my job as a supervisor, sure, but I can't say that I only eat like that when I'm feeling stressed or sad. It just kind of... happens. I haven't connected it to any particular feeling beforehand.
After these episodes of eating large amounts of food, how do you feel about yourself? And has this pattern of eating affected your daily life, work, relationships, or how you feel about your body?

Afterwards, I just feel... really ashamed. It's hard to deal with. And yes, it has definitely affected my daily life. I've actually stopped inviting people over to my house because of it. I just don't want anyone around. And I end up skipping my normal evening routines, too... like doing my yoga or going out to do my gardening chores. I just feel too ashamed and... preoccupied, I guess, after these episodes to really do much of anything else.

Over these past several months when you've been having these eating episodes multiple times a week, have you noticed changes in your weight? Has your weight gone up, stayed about the same, or changed in some other way?

I haven't really noticed any major changes in my weight, to be honest. I mean, I don't weigh myself every day or anything, but my clothes seem to fit about the same. So, I guess it's stayed pretty steady.

When you think back to one of these eating episodes, can you give me an example of the actual amount of food you ate? For instance, how many containers, or what would you estimate in terms of calories or meals' worth of food?

Well, um, that's actually why I came in. I keep having these evenings where... I'll stop and buy a whole family-size takeout order on the way home. And then I'll add a big bag of chips, or maybe some bakery things from the grocery store. And I'll eat almost all of it myself. It's like I don't even register how much food is actually gone until it's just... empty wrappers and containers everywhere.
